tools.name: get_shop_facts
tools.description: What variotrip is and how it works, in the shop’s own words: one mobile-data eSIM for the whole route, one shared data pool, the trip length, ranges, delivery, payment, hotspot, activation, top-ups (data, days or a country), router activation, e-mails, support. Use for any question that is not a pri

tools.name: list_destinations
tools.description: Every country variotrip can put on a route, with the number of selectable networks and the starting price of a one-country route (1 GB · 7 days · cheapest network). Use to check coverage or to see which countries of a trip are available.

tools.name: get_networks
tools.description: The mobile networks the customer can tick for one country (operator name, 4G/5G) with the price of a reference one-country route on each network alone (1 GB · 7 days), so you can say which network is the cheapest and what the others add.

tools.name: quote_route
tools.description: Use while the customer is still deciding — "how much is …?": the exact price of ONE eSIM for the whole route — the countries in travel order (1–8) with their networks, ONE data pool in GB for all of them and the trip length — the server price the customer would pay. A single country is a route of on

tools.name: recommend_config
tools.description: Use when the customer describes a trip instead of a size: the countries (with the days in each, when known) and how they use data (usage light / normal / heavy, or gb_per_day). Sizes the shared pool from the trip length and returns three server-quoted routes — exact, comfortable (×1.5) and generous

tools.name: price_grid
tools.description: The same route priced for several trip lengths (days, max 8) and several pool sizes (gb, max 6), in one call — e.g. to compare with other providers or to find the best fit. Same server prices as quote_route; each cell has its own buy_url.

tools.name: start_checkout
tools.description: Use only once the customer has decided to buy ("I'll take it", "how do I buy?"): the checkout handoff for one route (same input as quote_route). Returns the buy_url to give the customer, the final price and a ready-to-send checkout block (next_step, payment_methods, delivery) — on the page the route

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: start_checkout · Public sink: start_checkout.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: start_checkout · Public sink: start_checkout

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
